chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the crucified one [for prayer], so he said, 'Do you not know that my grandfather (peace be upon him) prayed over his uncle?' I said, 'I know that, but I do not understand it clearly.' He said, 'I will clarify it for you: If the face of the crucified one is towards the Qibla, stand on his right shoulder; and if his back is towards the Qibla, stand on his left shoulder, for between the East and the West is the Qibla. If his left shoulder is towards the Qibla, stand on his right shoulder; and if his right shoulder is towards the Qibla, stand on his left shoulder. And however he is turned, do not deviate from his shoulders, and let your face be towards what is between the East and the West, and do not face him directly nor have your back to him at all.' Abu Hashim said, 'And I have understood, if God wills, I have understood, by God.'

key_terms.الْمَصْلُوبِ: The crucified one (referring to the deceased fixed in a vertical position)

ai.seo_question: How to perform funeral prayer over a crucified person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the fiqh of praying over the crucified by establishing a geometric principle: the pray-er stands on the shoulder opposite the Qibla to ensure the face is oriented between East and West, avoiding direct facing or back-turning. This ruling, rooted in the precedent of the Prophet praying over his uncle Hamza, resolves the ambiguity of vertical orientation by prioritizing the pray-er's relative alignment with the Qibla rather than the body's fixed position.
